function: Predicts BS beamforming vectors (precoders) that maximize harvested energy under secrecy-capacity and transmit-power constraints in a multi-user SWIPT system (p. 1, 4, 7).
system: Multi-antenna BS (Nt=20), Nu=10 single-antenna ID nodes, L=3 EH-IoT nodes, K=4 eavesdroppers with Nr=2 antennas, no RIS; frequency band not stated (p. 3, 8).
method: Supervised FNN and CNN with custom output activation functions (EHBL, CBL) derived from the problem constraints; MSE loss, Adam; labels are SCA beamformers (p. 5, 7).
data_channel: Own simulated CSI sets (with large-scale fading, without, norm-bound error 0.1) labelled by the SCA solver; fading law unspecified; results over 10,000 samples (p. 7, 8, 10).
test_conditions: Trained on CSI with large-scale fading, without it, and with norm-bound error; power varied per training phase; Nt, Nu sweeps; no cross-condition test stated (p. 5, 8, 11).
baselines: Non-learned: SCA [12]. Learned: CNN with ReLU [23], DNN with DBL [24], DNN with Softmax [17], DRL [18] (p. 3, 8, 13).
metrics: Harvested energy (dBm) and secrecy capacity (bps/Hz) versus transmit power, Nt, Nu; energy-secrecy trade-off; computation time per sample (ms, s) (p. 8-13).
complexity: Orders O(Nu^2) DBL, O(L^2 Nt^3) EHBL, O(Nt^3 Nu^3 K) CBL for activation layers (p. 7); measured time per sample, e.g. CNN-CBL 183.4 ms, SCA 20.4 s at Nu=10 (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 8: "The CSI with large scale fading, the CSI without large scale fading, and the CSI with norm-bound errors are used to train the neural network models"; the fading model is not specified, and no standardized or measured channel is named.
q2_support: p. 5: "The transmit power P is varied for each training phase"; p. 11 sweeps Nt and Nu (scalability analysis), but no passage tests a model trained in one configuration on a configuration absent from its training.
q3_support: p. 3: "We have compared the DL methodologies with the successive convex approximation (SCA)-based optimization approach [12] and also with the other DL approaches [23], [24]"; Figs. 4-12 and Table II compare harvested energy and secrecy capacity for SCA, ReLU, DBL, Softmax and DRL.
q4_support: p. 12: "Table III compares the computational time per sample between EHBL, CBL schemes, ReLU, DBL, sofmax, DRL, and SCA methods"; p. 7 also gives the complexity orders of the activation layers.
q5_support: p. 7: "the outputs correspond to beamforming vectors obtained from the SCA algorithm"; the dataset is self-generated, with no code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Area 3: supervised DNN/CNN predicts BS beamformers (labels from SCA) under SWIPT harvested-energy and secrecy constraints. No RIS (IRS appears only in related work, p. 3). Tables II to IV were read from the page image (p. 13). Fig. 4 and later legends read from page images (p. 8, 9).
